observations:
All bechina-connected concept families in Torah #69 fall within four identifiable packages derived from the connected components of the bechina graph. No cluster of 3+ concepts was found that forms an independent bechina domain not already captured by one of those four packages.

The following candidate domains were examined:

1. KIDDUSHIN / BETROTHAL CLUSTER: The source text discusses kiddushin at length (lines 20-22), including the act of betrothal by money, the formula of the ketubah, and the mechanism by which the nefesh is extracted from among the klipot through the husband's giving of kessef. Surface candidates: קידושין, כֶּסֶף שֶׁל קִדּוּשִׁין, כְּתֻבָּה. However, this is not an independent domain — it is a concrete application of the ממון/נפש relationship. The Rebbe's entire discussion of kiddushin is explicitly framed as an EXAMPLE of how ממון completes the nefesh (Package 1 = wealth domain, Package 2 = soul/feminine domain). Kiddushin is the rite through which ממון fulfills its essential role; it is not a separate essential domain. The concept קידושין is flagged as a gap addition to Package 1 (not a new independent package).

2. BASELESS HATRED / SINAH CHINAM CLUSTER: The source text discusses at length how greed (תאוות ממון) leads to mental cloudiness (עכירת המח), which produces שׂוֹנְאִים and eventually שׂוֹנְאֵי חִנָּם (causeless haters coming from brain-overflow/שערות). Surface candidates: שׂוֹנְאֵי חִנָּם, שׂוֹנְאִים, עכירת המח. However: (a) שׂוֹנְאֵי חִנָּם is explicitly declared a bechina of שערות (Package 4) — it is a gap addition to that existing package, not an independent cluster. (b) שׂוֹנְאִים (plural) is mentioned as a consequence in eitza (causal) language, not as a bechina-equivalence. (c) עכירת המח is framed causally ('מֵחֲמַת שֶׁנָּפְסָק הַמֹּחַ, נוֹלָד הַשִּׂנְאָה'), not as a bechina-parallel of another concept. The hatred theme is entirely subsumed within the שערות/מחין cluster (Package 4) and its gap additions; it does not constitute a new independent package.

3. GAZLAN / THEFT-CONSEQUENCES CLUSTER: The Torah contains extensive discussion of the spiritual consequences of robbery — the robber takes the neighbor's soul-light, becomes attracted to the neighbor's wife, can lose his own wife, produces unfit children. Surface candidates: גַּזְלָן, גְּזֵלָה, חֶמְדָּה (covetousness — from the Ten Commandments 'לֹא תַחְמֹד'). However, none of these appear in explicit bechina language. The Rebbe uses 'בְּחִינַת' for the robber's action only to identify it with known concepts already in other packages (e.g., 'כְּאִלּוּ בָּא עַל אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ' is a Talmudic comparison, not a bechina declaration). The robber-theme is narrated in eitza (cause-and-effect) language throughout: stealing → attracts wife's soul-light → becomes drawn to her → potentially loses his own wife. This is the eitza flow BETWEEN packages, not a new bechina cluster.

4. RIGHT/LEFT STRUCTURAL DUALITY: תורה = ימין and ממון = שמאל appear together in Torah #69 (from Proverbs 3:16 and Ecclesiastes 10:2). One might propose a 'ימין/שמאל' meta-package. However, these two pairs are each absorbed into their respective content packages (Package 1 for ממון/שמאל, Package 3 for תורה/ימין) because in Torah #69 ימין and שמאל are not elaborated as an independent structural domain — they are mentioned once each as a proof-text identifier. The ימין/שמאל duality is a structural feature referenced briefly, not a developed bechina network.

Conclusion: The four packages identified — (1) מָמוֹן וְעֲנָפִים, (2) נֶפֶשׁ וּנְקֵבָה, (3) בָּנִים וְתוֹרָה, (4) שְׂעָרוֹת וּמֹחִין — fully account for all bechina-connected nodes in the dataset. Gap additions (torah_69_additions.json) extend existing packages but do not constitute new independent bechina domains. No additional package domain meeting the threshold of 3+ concepts forming a new independent bechina family is detectable from the source text.
